title: Meshy migrations dir is src-tauri/migrations (registry database.rs), commands registered in lib.rs
chosen: adapter/gates/scaffolds corrected to repo reality
why: verified by ls and include_str! in storage/database.rs; agent assumption was wrong
alternatives: keep agent paths

title: DRK-01 sweep excludes src/components/ui/** (shadcn primitives legitimately carry dark: variants)
chosen: exclude ui primitives and tests
why: audit mode flagged 8+ hits in badge/button/checkbox ui primitives
alternatives: leave failing

title: ADR-0015 (accepted, merged #13) supersedes remediation WUs C/D/E as originally scoped
chosen: restructured to ADR-0015 steps: snap-rust (step1), taskType+snapshot dispatch (step2), artifacts in save/download (step3)
why: poll_task/stream_task/save_completed_task changes are exactly ADR-0015 scope; plan must follow the accepted ADR, not restate it
alternatives: execute original WU-C/D/E

title: WU-A lands RED guardrail before fixes; CommandName union is hand-maintained mirror of generate_handler!
chosen: typed invoke + ipc-contract.guardrail.test.ts parsing both lib.rs blocks; phantom commands stay red until WU-B
why: fail-before-fix evidence required by orchestrator gates; union set-equality test prevents drift
alternatives: runtime-only check

title: TaskSnapshot dropped_fields policy (WU-SNAP)
chosen: dropped_fields: Vec<String> on TaskSnapshot with #[serde(skip)]; texture_urls deliberately stay in providerPayload until ADR-0015 step 3; presetClip labels sanitized via sanitize_cache_key rules
why: test-visible per TPC-03 without serializing to IPC; IPC-06 names-only; texture save keys are step-3 scope
alternatives: separate debug return type

title: WU-B flips guardrail green; ExportDialog plugin-dialog exception closed via saveFileDialog
chosen: settings.rs commands with key allowlist; openFileDialog/saveFileDialog in tauri.ts as sole dialog importers
why: pre-existing direct save import contradicted the boundary rule the same wave enforces; closing it costs 3 small edits
alternatives: document as exception

title: WU-D lands ADR-0015 step 2; transitional providerPayload reads marked
chosen: poll/stream/delete dispatch by taskType fail-closed; TaskSnapshot across IPC; legacy download/save rebuilt from artifacts with primary-wins
why: step 3 (artifact-native save/download args) deliberately deferred to WU-E per ADR follow-up order
alternatives: combine steps 2+3
undo: revert steps 2-3 together per ADR Undo section

title: WU-E lands ADR-0015 step 3: artifact-native save_completed_task/download_asset, TASK-0031 closed
chosen: SaveCompletedTaskArgs struct param (frontend sends {args:{...}}, verified against tauri 2.11.5 CommandItem payload.get(key)); artifact_storage_key/artifact_filename closed (role,format) mapping in validation.rs; download-all-or-INVALID_INPUT; has_rig/has_animation derived from roles/task type
why: TPC-04 requires role-tagged backward-compatible keys and the TASK-0031 gate forbids silent artifact drops; a format->url map cannot hold both
alternatives: keep flattened params + loose artifacts Vec arg; skip has_animation derivation
undo: revert with step-2 range per ADR Undo; role-keyed rows stay readable (primary keys unchanged)

title: WU-F: AssetRow file_paths/texture_paths/tags typed across IPC
chosen: HashMap/Vec/Vec deserialize in from_row, malformed degrades to empty with log::warn; tags included (same defect class); texture keys unreshaped
why: components were JSON.parse-ing storage blobs at three sites; all writers verified to emit object/array JSON so both storage eras read cleanly
alternatives: frontend parse helper

title: WU-G wires SSE into useActiveTaskPolling; useTaskStream deleted; interval stays as safety net
chosen: per-task stream_task + task-progress/task-complete listeners, health window pollIntervalMs x3, always-on interval skipping healthy tasks, single savedTaskIds dedup
why: settings toggle promised SSE with no implementation; one orchestrator owns save/download pipeline (F4 dedup); double-mount in TaskMonitor would have doubled streams
alternatives: keep orphan hook + consumer

title: D-011 get_all_tags command: tag dropdown stops fetching every asset row
chosen: new #[tauri::command] get_all_tags returning DISTINCT names via INNER JOIN tags/asset_tags ORDER BY name; useAllTags hook reduced to a single invoke; registered in lib.rs + tauri.ts CommandName union
why: useAllTags built the dropdown by invoking get_all_assets and reducing client-side, so the whole assets table (prompts, notes, file_paths/texture_paths blobs) crossed IPC for a list of short strings; dedupe belongs in SQL
alternatives: keep client-side reduce; expose tags from the already-typed AssetRow without a new command

title: D-012 DAT-01 pagination: list_assets_page/search_assets_page + useInfiniteAssets
chosen: bounded LIMIT/OFFSET with validate_page_window at the boundary (max 500, default 50); AssetPage{assets,total,limit,offset} across IPC; new useInfiniteAssets drives Load More; useAssets kept unpaged for client-side-filtering consumers
why: DAT-01 specifies pages of 50 and no query had any LIMIT; but AssetTaskPicker/AssetDetail/generate panels need the FULL set, so paginating useAssets would silently hide eligible tasks (e.g. a rig older than page 1)
alternatives: paginate useAssets for all callers (breaks client-side filters); virtualize-only via RND-03 without bounded SQL (leaves the IPC payload unbounded)

title: D-013 paging tiebreaker: ORDER BY created_at DESC, id ASC
chosen: add id ASC as a tiebreaker in list_assets_page, search_assets_windowed and count_assets; total returned instead of inferring hasNextPage from a short page
why: created_at is provider-supplied and collides across tasks; with an ambiguous ORDER BY SQLite may vary row order between queries, so offset paging could show one row twice and never show another. A short page also cannot detect the end when the last page is exactly full
alternatives: keyset/cursor paging on (created_at,id) in the response envelope (needs an opaque cursor across IPC); hasNextPage from returned<limit

title: D-014 migration 003: composite index for the paged ORDER BY (finding P-01)
chosen: CREATE INDEX idx_assets_created_id ON assets(created_at DESC, id ASC); additive only, no DROP of idx_assets_created; registered as MIGRATIONS entry 3
why: the id ASC tiebreaker added by D-013 for deterministic offset paging made SQLite emit USE TEMP B-TREE FOR RIGHT PART OF ORDER BY, sorting the whole table before returning page 1 (measured 1.053ms vs 92.4us on 2000 rows, exact shipping query); dropping the now-redundant idx_assets_created is a separate destructive decision the composite does not require
alternatives: drop the id tiebreaker (reintroduces the duplicate/skipped-row paging bug); keyset paging (deviates from DAT-01, needs an ADR); leave the sorter (11x on page 1)
undo: git revert; migration is additive so a reverted binary still opens the v3 file (schema_version 3 > 2, no pending migration)

title: D-015 BPR-01/BPR-02/BPR-03 pragmas and HTTP pool limit (findings P-06/P-07/P-08)
chosen: PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL and PRAGMA cache_size = -64000 in Database::open (file-backed path only, matching journal_mode); .pool_max_idle_per_host(5) on the MeshyClient builder
why: citing the rule text: BPR-01 asks for WAL + synchronous=NORMAL (synchronous was left at SQLite default FULL, an fsync per commit); BPR-02 asks for a 64MB cache; BPR-03 asks for pool_max_idle_per_host=5. All three were absent by construction
alternatives: leave synchronous at FULL (safe but pays an fsync per write); set cache_size in pages; add the pool limit to the download client too (separate client, deliberately not changed here)

title: D-016 recovery test re-pointed after migration 003 changed which failure a spoofed backup hits
chosen: restore_rejects_spoofed_schema_that_skips_migrations now derives the at-or-above-latest version from latest_schema_version() instead of hardcoding 2, and a new test covers the cannot-be-migrated case asserting BACKUP_MIGRATION_FAILED
why: the old hardcoded version 2 stopped being exactly-current once 003 existed, so run_migrations attempted 003 against a two-column assets table and restore failed closed as BACKUP_MIGRATION_FAILED rather than BACKUP_SCHEMA_MISMATCH. Fail-closed behavior is unchanged (live DB byte-identical, nothing quarantined), so only the test expectation was wrong; deriving from latest_schema_version() stops it silently rotting at the next migration
alternatives: loosen the assertion to accept either error; make 003 tolerant of a missing created_at column

title: D-014 migration 003: composite index for the paged ORDER BY (finding P-01)
chosen: CREATE INDEX idx_assets_created_id ON assets(created_at DESC, id ASC); additive only, no DROP of idx_assets_created; registered as MIGRATIONS entry 3

title: D-017 P-05: patch cached asset rows instead of blanket-invalidating the asset key family
chosen: one shared src/hooks/assetQueryKeys.ts owning the key family; patchCachedAssets iterates the cache by prefix and writes the delta into loaded rows; invalidateAssetLists/invalidateAllTags for membership changes; toggle_favorite/update_notes/update_tags/download_asset patch, delete_asset patches then invalidates, save_completed_task invalidates lists and tags
why: invalidateQueries matches by PREFIX, so queryKey [assets] hit every assets all entry plus every assets page filter entry: measured with the old key, a mutation matched 3 cached queries (3 refetches); with the patch the same 3 entries update with 0 fetches. Also fixes a separate defect: nothing invalidated all-tags, so the tag filter went stale after a tag edit
alternatives: keep blanket invalidation (N refetches per edit); recompute all pages client-side on every mutation; optimistic onMutate (a pattern used nowhere in this repo)

title: D-018 P-10: stream downloads to disk with a 2 GiB cap (BPR-04)
chosen: download_file delegates to download_file_capped with MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES=2GiB; chunked write via response.bytes_stream(); Content-Length pre-check AND running-total check; partial file deleted on every failure path; new MeshyError/ProviderError::DownloadTooLarge mapped to DOWNLOAD_TOO_LARGE at the IPC edge
why: client.rs did response.bytes().await then fs::write, buffering a whole model in memory; security_threat_model.md cites BPR-04 as an implemented DoS control, so the documented posture was false. 2GiB is far above any plausible Meshy asset (Rigging input ceiling 300k faces) so it cannot reject a legitimate model. The cap is a parameter so enforcement is testable without a 2GiB fixture
alternatives: stream without a cap (satisfies BPR-04 literally, still fills the disk); correct only the threat-model doc and leave the code; make the limit user-configurable

title: D-019 park P-02 virtualization and P-04 orphan cleanup pending an owner decision
chosen: leave both unimplemented; recorded as open Tier 3 items in docs/audits/perf-findings-asset-read-path-2026-11-08.md
why: P-02 requires adding @tanstack/react-virtual, where DEP-04/PR-06 justification is the owner call rather than a side effect of a perf sweep; P-04 deletes user files on disk and needs a product rule for whether a task id still referenced is safe to sweep. Both are explicitly owner decisions under this repo governance, so proceeding autonomously would exceed the mandate
alternatives: add the dependency and virtualize; conservative 24h-age sweep; user-triggered cleanup in Settings
